about.title: About ChobiKit
body: ChobiKit ("chobi" means picture in Bengali) is a collection of free image tools that run entirely in your own browser. There is no server doing the work — when you compress, convert or resize a photo, your own phone or computer does it, using the same technology that renders web pages.

We built ChobiKit because most online image tools upload your photos to a server first. That is slow, it eats your mobile data, and it means your private photos pass through someone else's computer. ChobiKit works the opposite way: the tool comes to you, and your files stay with you.
ChobiKit is made for everyone, with special care for users in Bangladesh and India — it is fully translated into Bengali, works well on mid-range phones, and costs nothing.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: The short version: your images never leave your device.

When you use any ChobiKit tool, your files are processed locally by your own browser. No image, video or file content is ever uploaded, stored or sent to us or to anyone else. The tools even keep working if you go offline after the page has loaded.
We do not use accounts, cookies, or tracking that identifies you. We do not collect your files, your names, or your email addresses.

If analytics are enabled on this site, they use a privacy-friendly, cookie-free service that only records anonymous page-view counts — never file names, file contents, or anything you do inside a tool. Analytics can be switched off entirely.
In short: what happens on your device stays on your device.

terms.title: Terms of Use
body: ChobiKit is provided free of charge, for anyone to use, as it is. There are no accounts and no agreements to sign.

The tools run on your own device and depend on your device's browser, memory and speed. Results may vary between devices and browsers, and very large files may fail on devices with limited memory. Please keep backups of anything important — you are responsible for your own files.
The site is offered without any warranty. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the ChobiKit team is not liable for any loss or damage resulting from the use of the site or its tools.
You agree not to use ChobiKit for anything unlawful, and not to attempt to interfere with the site's operation.
These terms may be updated from time to time; the latest version will always be on this page.

items.question: Are my images uploaded anywhere?
items.answer: No. All compression happens inside your browser, on your own device. You can even turn off your internet after the page loads — the tool keeps working.

items.question: How much smaller will my images get?
items.answer: It depends on each image. Photos often shrink 60–90% with little visible change. For an exact size, use the "Make it under ___ KB" target mode.

items.question: Will compression reduce the quality?
items.answer: A little, depending on the quality slider. Around 80 the difference is usually invisible; lower values give smaller files with more visible loss.

items.question: Which formats can I compress?
items.answer: JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF output, plus HEIC (iPhone), GIF and BMP input. You can keep the original format or pick another one.

items.question: Are my images uploaded anywhere?
items.answer: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser. Nothing is sent to any server, and the tool even works offline once loaded.

items.question: Which formats can I convert between?
items.answer: Output: JPG, PNG, WebP and AVIF. Input: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (first frame), BMP and HEIC/HEIF photos from iPhone.

items.question: Why do I need a background color for JPG?
items.answer: JPG cannot store transparency, so transparent areas need a color behind them. White is used by default — pick another color if you like.

items.question: What is HEIC?
items.answer: The photo format iPhones use by default. Convert HEIC to JPG here to share it anywhere without extra apps.

items.question: Are my images uploaded anywhere?
items.answer: No. Resizing happens on your own device, inside your browser. No uploads, no accounts.

items.question: What do Cover and Contain mean?
items.answer: With a preset: Cover fills the size completely and crops the edges; Contain fits the whole image inside, which may leave empty space.

items.question: What does the lock button do?
items.answer: It keeps the width-to-height ratio: change the width and the height follows automatically. Unlock to set them independently.

items.question: Why does the result have a size in its name?
items.answer: So you can tell apart multiple resized copies, e.g. photo-800x600.jpg.
